summary:
This bill tells the President to remove United States soldiers from fighting in or against Iran. Congress is the part of the government that has the power to declare war. Congress has not declared war on Iran. The President started using military force against Iran on February 28, 2026, and told Congress on March 2, 2026. A law called the War Powers Resolution says the President must stop using the military within 60 days unless Congress approves. The 60 days end on May 1, 2026.

If this bill becomes law, the President would have to pull U.S. troops out of the fighting in Iran unless Congress officially votes to allow the war. However, the bill says the United States can still do some things. The military can still defend against attacks on U.S. people or buildings in other countries. The U.S. can still gather and share information about threats from Iran. It can still help Israel and other countries defend themselves. It can also still help U.S. citizens leave the area safely.
